answer:
Your records list two medicines as active right now:

1. Atorvastatin 20 mg tablet: one tablet by mouth once a day. This is a statin for cholesterol.
2. Jardiance (empagliflozin) 10 mg tablet: one tablet by mouth once a day, in the morning. This is for type 2 diabetes.

Metformin 500 mg is marked as stopped, with an end date of 15 April 2024. Your records give the prescription date for the two current medicines (20 February 2025) but not the date you started taking them. Please check this list with your pharmacy or doctor. Include any over-the-counter medicines or supplements, which may not be in these records.
short: Active per records: atorvastatin 20 mg once daily and Jardiance 10 mg each morning. Metformin was stopped in April 2024. Please confirm with your pharmacy.

items.says: Atorvastatin 20 mg tablet, one tablet by mouth once daily, is listed as active.
items.why: It is the only statin in her records and is marked active by the hospital record.

facts.says: Atorvastatin 20 mg tablet: take 1 tablet by mouth once daily
facts.name: Atorvastatin 20 mg tablet

knowledge.says: A statin lowers LDL cholesterol and reduces cardiovascular risk. It is usually taken once a day, at any time.

items.says: Jardiance (empagliflozin) 10 mg tablet, one tablet by mouth once daily in the morning, is listed as active.
items.why: The hospital record marks it active, and it was prescribed on 20 February 2025.

facts.says: Jardiance 10 mg tablet: take 1 tablet by mouth once daily in the morning
facts.name: Jardiance 10 mg tablet

knowledge.says: Jardiance is an SGLT2 inhibitor that lowers blood sugar and also helps protect the heart and kidneys. Tell your doctor about genital or urinary infections, or dizziness while taking it.
knowledge.guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes (SGLT2 inhibitors in type 2 diabetes).

items.says: Metformin 500 mg tablet is not current. Its record shows it was completed and ended on 15 April 2024.
items.why: Her records show no metformin after April 2024, and the medicine is not on her active list.

knowledge.says: Metformin is a common first treatment for type 2 diabetes. Records do not say why it was stopped, so ask your doctor if you are unsure.

links.says: Metformin ended in April 2024, about ten months before Jardiance was prescribed; the records do not link the two.
